name: Artizon Museum
funding: Run by the Ishibashi Foundation, set up in 1956 by Bridgestone founder Shojiro Ishibashi, who gave it his art collection. Known as the Bridgestone Museum of Art before.

name: Japan Folk Crafts Museum (Nihon Mingeikan)
funding: 2025: public-interest foundation chaired by Naoto Fukasawa, run on admissions, members' dues (corporate from JPY 100k) and donations; no roster published.

name: Mori Art Museum
funding: Corporate endowment from Mori Building Co., Shiseido, corporate sponsors.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo
funding: Tokyo Metropolitan Government museum; budget about ¥1B.

name: NTT InterCommunication Center (ICC)
funding: Corporate cultural facility (2026) run and paid for by NTT East, a telecom operator, in Tokyo Opera City Tower.

name: Nezu Museum
funding: Chairman Koichi Nezu is honorary chairman of Tobu Department Store; councillor Yoshizumi Nezu chairs Tobu Railway.

name: Tokyo Arts and Space
funding: Its 2026 shows are run and paid for by the Tokyo Metropolitan Foundation for History and Culture (Tokyo government). The Korean Embassy and Cultural Center back one show.

name: Watari-um
funding: Private museum that opened in September 1990. It sells shop, art pass and support memberships.

name: Towada Art Center
funding: Municipal museum run for Towada City by Nanjo and Associates Group. August 2026 corporate members include Towada Gas. City FY2018 records show ¥17.7M siting funds and a ¥5M grant.

name: Yamaguchi Center for Arts and Media (YCAM)
funding: FY2021 programme budget ¥305M: 88.7% Yamaguchi City, 3.3% Agency for Cultural Affairs grants. The 2026 show is funded by the same two.

name: Yokohama Museum of Art
funding: FY2024 income ¥1.10B: ¥881M city management fee through the Yokohama Arts Foundation, ¥91M own projects, ¥23M fees, ¥40M city support. Five HEART to ART corporate partners.

name: Amman Design Week
funding: Founded 2016 by Queen Rania; organised with Greater Amman Municipality. 2016 sponsors: Al Manaseer Group, Zain, Aramex, Al Markaziya. 2026: Sukhtian Foundation backs the student exhibition.
